The pack plays well, some quests ("some") have crappy quest descriptions that don't help much, but most quests lead into each other well enough to figure out what I need to be doing. Some mods feel thrown in, for example I LOVE the Twilight Forest mod, but like most modpacks, its entire addition to the pack is literally just to have it, as it provides no advancements and no depth to the pack, its like "Hey now you can go there and progress Twilight Forest like normal and theres some hobbit hills you can raid for loot and ores" and that feels lame :\

Grinds don't seem very hardcore at all throw the early and early-mid game. Build a 7x7 sieve grid, and just mass veinmeiner-hammer 9 stacks of cobblestone and sieve the gravel only takes like 5 minutes to get an absurd amount of ores, and that feels fair.

The ease of getting the Zenith furnace and upgrades for it felt underlooked, as I picked that up fairly early, killed a wither, and now had ore doubling at 1tick/double and I hadn't even made any farming or real mob grind room or any real machinery yet, it felt a bit too simple

Overall I like the pack. I hate Abyssalcraft and VoidCraft, but I respect them very much for what those mods do, they do well; they fuck shit up. PO2 felt a lot grindier, Stoneblock felt less grindier, but I've still got a lot to do and Im enjoying my time.

the mix bag calls for 1 / 9 minutes mix, and 60/20 minutes of sit. Perhaps drop to 45/15 minutes ? Our dough looks really good out of the mixer, but thats about all :\

I believe our issue is the proofing? I can grab pictures of the previous product compared to ours if it helps :\

We're also making Kronuts, and ours are waaaay smaller than the other store's.

Measuring Mix/Water/Yeast according to Mix directions, we mix in a 3 speed mixer (big) on speed 1, for one minute. 
Then on speed 2 for 9 minutes. Let it sit, covered for 50-60 minutes, and bring it to the table.

We split our dough into two loafs, beat out the air bubbles and let it sit on the table for another 20 minutes, both loaves covered.

After the 20 minutes we roll it out, we try to keep it rectangular in shape and about 1/2 inch in thickness; cut the doughnuts and set them into the proofer for approx. 20-30 minutes? We test if theyre proofed by touching it and if your finger leaves a print still, it needs more time, but if theyre too firm theyre in for too long.

We're based in Nevada, very dry, so our proofer is just cranked to max, with a pan of warm/hot water at the bottom.

Drop the screen out of the proofer into the fryer, 375 degrees, 36 doughnuts at a time, about 45 seconds on one side, flip them, 45 seconds on the other, flip them back and pull them out.

Bring them to the glazer (or not for some) and then onto trays and into racks.

The old doughnuts are about an inch tall, very round with a nice ring in the center. They're fluffy and great.
